content_text: Operators often want a “surround” view on their eyepiece or monitor to see what’s just out of frame to know what to avoid (or what to include) before it encroaches on the shot. Same can be helpful for focus pullers and DPs, or really anyone on set watching a monitor. Sure, it could be distracting at first, but it’s easy to get used to. Most monitors allow you to grey out or otherwise diminish the image outside the frame lines, but its rarely useful to fully black it out.
